## Functions

### `captureRealmLifecycleCompositionTelemetrySource(...args)`

Capture the host-private telemetry source of the original six-field lifecycle composition. Copies, facades and proxies cannot substitute for that original. The frozen { capture } companion grants observation only, not owner acquisition, dispatch, resource or lifecycle authority. Lookup remains stable after closure; work capture/currentness do not. Teardown keeps its original root validator.

### `captureRealmLifecycleCompositionOwnerBinding(...args)`

Authenticate one original issuer-created owner companion without reflecting on it or accepting a registration writer. Copies, proxies and matching labels cannot substitute. Historical lookup grants no currentness: its original operations retain their existing work and teardown checks.

### `captureRealmLifecycleCompositionAttemptSource(...args)`

Kernel-private capture of the original composition's bound attempt roots. The frozen { capture, assertOperatorContext } companion forwards through the composition operation fence and original allocation source. Capture accepts exactly frozen { signal }; the guard authenticates the exact coordinator object without inspecting its fields or returning the original coordinator. Its stable five-field result identifies the original operator and live native construction/work/teardown roots before allocation. It is not a session, lifecycle-generation or ongoing currentness receipt; no context or storage escapes. Lookup is historical, while capture rejects closing/closed sources.

### `captureRealmLifecycleCompositionObservationSource(...args)`

Kernel-private read-only observation of an original issued lifecycle. capture accepts the exact frozen five-field currentness request, including the original work root. The stable binding has only a native invalidation signal and a zero-argument currentness check. First admitted close invalidates it even when cleanup must be retried; neither invalidation nor lookup proves retirement or resource cleanup. No caller root or public lifecycle wire is changed.

### `createRealmLifecyclePortComposition(options)`

Own one genuine lifecyclePort@1 and its three Kernel source leases. Exact frozen options are { operatorContext, generationStorageView, appId }. The genuine allocation, identity and participant authorities are constructed in that order. Construction reserves no generation and performs no storage I/O; only the participant source subscribes to its original operator context. Output is exactly frozen { lifecyclePort, attemptBinding, hostLifecycle, ownerIdentity, observeRetirement, close }. Only lifecyclePort enters the existing sixteen-dependency record. Its frozen realmLifecycle@1 wire retains the four existing methods and mutable request semantics. The same-wire attemptBinding@1 forwarder belongs to the separate host mount context. The raw hostLifecycle@1 source belongs to the approved v3 channel wrapper. ownerIdentity is a host-private { acquire, authenticate } forwarding facade, not a genuine identity source for private lookup and not processOwnerPort@1. Its original authentic owner handles retain release authority for cleanup. observeRetirement is host-private observation, never another app port method. These do not implement process children, resource accounting or activation. A separate private lookup derives telemetry from the original identity source without making this facade a genuine identity source. Its capture and current checks share the synchronous operation fence. Retained teardown checks bypass the work fence, but successful full close requires their root already aborted. close() is synchronous, zero-argument and idempotent after success. Its first admitted call fences all new attempts, allocation, currentness, participant registration and owner acquisition/authentication, then closes participant, identity and allocation sources in reverse creation order. Each source must meet its existing cleanup prerequisites. A failed step reports CLEANUP_REQUIRED and retains both completed steps and remaining sources for an explicit retry. Retirement and observation remain available until allocation closure; pending allocation promises are returned unchanged and may still issue genuine handles needed for that cleanup. First admission synchronously notifies the private observation signal after its fences are committed, before child cleanup. No close call aborts Entry's roots, retires generations, releases owners, disposes participants or asynchronously awaits Entry/adapter callbacks. Synchronous forwarded operations fence reentrant close before closure starts, so a newly issued cleanup handle cannot be hidden by a post-operation failure. Recursive close during child closure is rejected separately. The attempt forwarder prohibits binding fresh roots once closure starts. Host terminal notifications remain available until the participant source itself closes. Successful closure proves only these three source leases ended, not boot-owned operator-transition drain, resource cleanup, provider isolation or city rendering.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
